content: If you miss a dose of this medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and proceed with your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to make up for the missed one. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not freeze it. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not dispose of this medication by flushing it down the toilet or pouring it into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed, following local waste disposal regulations. This information was last revised in May 2024. It is important to note that this document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Take this medication by mouth as directed, either as needed or according to the instructions provided by your doctor or the product packaging. The dosage is determined based on your age, medical condition, and response to treatment. Do not increase your dose or take this medication more frequently than directed. Do not exceed the recommended dose for your age. If you are using chewable tablets, chew each tablet thoroughly before swallowing. If you are using the liquid form, shake the bottle well before each dose and measure the dose carefully using a special measuring device or cup. This medication may interact with other drugs, such as tetracycline antibiotics or chloroquine, potentially reducing their absorption. If your doctor has instructed you to use this medication daily, take it regularly to achieve the maximum benefit. Inform your doctor if your condition persists or worsens. Side effects from this medication are rare. The most common side effects include darkening of the stools and/or tongue. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, it is because they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Persistent vomiting or diarrhea may lead to dehydration. Rarely, this medication may cause serious, potentially fatal bleeding in the stomach or intestines. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are also rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking bismuth subsalicylate, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, aspirin, salicylates (e.g., salsalate), NSAIDs (e.g., ibuprofen, naproxen, celecoxib), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. This medication may also contain aspartame. It contains a salicylate, which is similar to aspirin. Children and teenagers under 18 years of age should not take this product if they have chickenpox, flu, or any undiagnosed illness, or if they have recently received a vaccine. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. This medication may harm an unborn baby and cause complications with normal labor or delivery. It is not recommended for use during pregnancy from 20 weeks until delivery. If your doctor determines that you need to use this medication between 20 and 30 weeks of pregnancy, use the lowest effective dose for the shortest possible time. Do not use this medication after 30 weeks of pregnancy. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk, but similar drugs do and may have undesirable effects on a nursing infant. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may increase the risk of bleeding when taken with other drugs that also increase bleeding risk. Carefully check the labels of all prescription and non-prescription medications, as many contain pain relievers or fever reducers (e.g., NSAIDs such as aspirin, ibuprofen, or naproxen) that are similar to this drug and may increase your risk of side effects if taken together. However, if your doctor has instructed you to take low-dose aspirin to prevent heart attack or stroke (usually 81-162 milligrams per day), continue taking the aspirin unless your doctor advises otherwise. This medication may interfere with certain medical or laboratory tests, such as X-rays of the intestines using contrast dye, potentially causing false test results. If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. If you are taking this medication for diarrhea, ensure you drink plenty of water to reduce the risk of dehydration.
